subproblem.title: Continuity of the rescaled integrals ∫ f d(ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ)) in the parameters (x, λ), λ > 0, for a finite μ₀ and continuous compactly supported f (parent step 5a)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ₀ a measure on ℝ^P with μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with compact support, and x_i ∈ ℝ^P, λ_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ), x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 with x_i → x and λ_i → λ. Then ∫ f d(ofReal(λ_i⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x_i λ_i)) → ∫ f d(ofReal(λ⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map(dilation x λ)) as i → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ₀ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (xs : ℕ → Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), μ₀ univ ≠ ∞ → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → (∀ i, 0 < lams i) → 0 < lam → Tendsto xs atTop (𝓝 x) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 lam) → Tendsto (fun i => ∫ v, f v ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((lams i)⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation (xs i) (lams i)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ v, f v ∂(ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • μ₀.map (dilation x lam))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 5a (continuity in the parameters via integral_smul_measure, integral_map and dominated convergence), in the sequential form used by parent step 5c and stated for an arbitrary finite measure μ₀.
Notation: η_{a,s} := dilation a s, so η_{a,s}(u) = −(s⁻¹•a) + s⁻¹•u = s⁻¹•(u − a) (definition of dilation and dilationCLM); η_{a,s} is continuous, hence measurable.
1. (Integral formula.) For a ∈ ℝ^P and s > 0: ∫ f d(ofReal(s⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map η_{a,s}) = (ofReal(s⁻¹^n)).toReal·∫ f d(μ₀.map η_{a,s}) (integral_smul_measure) = s⁻¹^n·∫ f(η_{a,s}(v)) dμ₀(v), by ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (s⁻¹^n ≥ 0) and integral_map (η_{a,s} is measurable and f is continuous, hence strongly measurable). We apply this with (a, s) = (x_i, λ_i) and with (a, s) = (x, λ).
2. (Scalar factors.) λ_i → λ ≠ 0, so λ_i⁻¹ → λ⁻¹ (continuity of inversion away from 0; Tendsto.inv₀) and λ_i⁻¹^n → λ⁻¹^n (Tendsto.pow).
3. (Pointwise convergence.) For each v ∈ ℝ^P: η_{x_i,λ_i}(v) = λ_i⁻¹•(v − x_i) → λ⁻¹•(v − x) = η_{x,λ}(v), by step 2, x_i → x and continuity of subtraction and scalar multiplication (Tendsto.sub, Tendsto.smul). Since f is continuous, g_i(v) := f(η_{x_i,λ_i}(v)) → g(v) := f(η_{x,λ}(v)).
4. (Domination.) A continuous function with compact support is bounded: there is C ∈ ℝ with |f(y)| ≤ C for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). Hence |g_i(v)| ≤ C for all i and v. The constant C is μ₀-integrable because μ₀ is finite (μ₀(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞). Each g_i is continuous (a composition of continuous maps), hence AE-strongly measurable.
5. (Dominated convergence.) By steps 3 and 4 and the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ g_i dμ₀ → ∫ g dμ₀.
6. (Conclusion.) By step 1, the i-th integral equals λ_i⁻¹^n·∫ g_i dμ₀ and the limit integral equals λ⁻¹^n·∫ g dμ₀. By steps 2 and 5 and continuity of multiplication (Tendsto.mul), λ_i⁻¹^n·∫ g_i dμ₀ → λ⁻¹^n·∫ g dμ₀. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∫ f d(ofReal(s⁻¹^n)•μ₀.map η_{a,s}) = s⁻¹^n·∫ f∘η_{a,s} dμ₀ for s > 0.
λ_i⁻¹^n → λ⁻¹^n and f(η_{x_i,λ_i}(v)) → f(η_{x,λ}(v)) pointwise.
f is bounded and μ₀ finite, so dominated convergence gives convergence of ∫ f∘η_{x_i,λ_i} dμ₀; multiply the limits.

audit.reason: The integral transformation is valid for the continuous maps involved. Compact support bounds f uniformly, and finite seed mass makes that bound integrable. Pointwise convergence, dominated convergence, and convergence of the positive-scale factors prove the exact sequential statement.
